A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-injected Deep InfoMax work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the additional Appendices E–F in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original MNIST normality, classification and clustering experiments, CIFAR-10/100 linear-probing results, and conditional and unconditional generation examples in Appendix D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds CIFAR-10 representation analyses and ImageNet-100/1k linear-probing results.

M1.justification: The proposed normalization, independent noise injection and InfoMax objective remain unchanged. The ResNet architectures and two-dimensional projection in the new experiments configure evaluations of the existing method; the expanded uniform-matching explanation does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluations on ImageNet-100 and ImageNet-1k, substantially extending the represented natural-image populations beyond MNIST and CIFAR-10/100. The additional two-dimensional CIFAR-10 experiments use an already covered dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same SimCLR and VICReg comparisons and noise variants. The MNIST downstream classifiers are also retained. The added experiments reuse existing methods without introducing a new competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix E introduces two-dimensional ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 evaluations over eight noise settings, with 400-epoch training and additional 800-epoch visualizations at a higher learning rate. Appendix F adds 100-epoch ImageNet evaluations using ResNet-18/50 and linear probing. These are new protocols, not revisions to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests Gaussianization and downstream performance through a CIFAR-10 noise sweep, normality tests, k-nearest-neighbor ROC AUC, and noise-free versus noisy embedding visualizations. Figures 5–7 also examine embeddings under two learning-rate/training-duration configurations, substantially extending the previous MNIST sensitivity evidence.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly documents five random seeds for the new CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments and adds uncertainty reporting to ImageNet linear probing. Table 2 does not identify what its ± values represent. The original MNIST five-run, 99% confidence-interval reporting remains unchanged; no increase in repetitions of retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports ImageNet results, including VICReg ImageNet-1k top-1 accuracy of 67.41% at zero noise and 67.19% at sigma = 0.2. Figures 5–7 add CIFAR-10 embedding and normality/classification findings. These are newly evaluated settings; the original CIFAR-10/100 Table 1 scores remain identical.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Gaussian and uniform matching theorems, dual formulation, and proofs in Appendices A–B are retained. V2 adds explanatory prose around existing results and renumbers equations, without changing the formal mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the same claims about automatic distribution matching, compatibility with information-based representation learning, and the downstream-performance trade-off. The added experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of how signal-to-noise ratio balances matching against augmentation invariance. Section 5 qualifies the earlier claim that accuracy does not drop to acknowledge slight drops, and interprets them through representation bandwidth and dimensionality.

D1.justification: Appendices E–F substantially expand implementation documentation: encoder and projection-head architectures, non-affine normalization, placement of noise relative to augmentation, noise grids, learning rates, training durations, and ImageNet batch-size and optimizer settings. Existing Appendix C details and the supplementary-source-code statement are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bazarova et al. on change-point detection, Lavoie et al. on simplicial embeddings, Russakovsky et al. for ImageNet, and da Costa et al. for solo-learn. These provide limited application, interpretation and implementation context; the overall novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands the noise and uniform-matching explanations, updates experimental paragraphs, adds Appendices E–F, and corrects an author name and contact text. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the empirical displays with ImageNet Table 2 and CIFAR-10 Figures 5–7. It also revises Figure 1's capacity-axis label and caption, relocates the existing tables, and places the unchanged generation Figures 3–4 together. The architecture table is renumbered from 2 to 3.

improvement.justification: V2 extends v1's MNIST distribution checks to CIFAR-10 and adds ImageNet classification evidence, with useful training and seed details. This strengthens empirical support. The gain remains limited because the ImageNet experiments do not measure distribution-matching quality, and Table 2 leaves its uncertainty statistic undefined.
